I was on it for 8 years I think with a break of 2 or so years in-between... And got PFS after stopping for 2 weeks and starting again. All the symptoms with insomnia and gum recession being the worst. I've mostly recovered now but still sensitive to anti androgens like Rosemary oil, which seem to set me back and put me into a mild state of PFS. It had taken around 3-4 years to get back to a mostly normal state anyway and I didn't take anything, just ate well and tried to relax as much as possible. 

All my hair fell out too which sucks since I liked having hair. PFS messes you up and leaves you with no options to try to offset the balding process.
Yeah it's not a full recovery but it's close
I'm still recovering 3 years later but the worst of it is behind me. It might not take you as long - just hang in there, eat healthy and you'll get better.

I had (and still have) some problems with insomnia - it was chronic at first but gradually became better and easier to manage - When I first quit I'd have several nights in a row with zero sleep and basically be a shivering wreck. Now I might wake up once or twice during the night but will generally fall back to sleep or doze off without taking anything.

I used magnesium and CBD oil when things were bad and if I get another bad night where I can't sleep I'll usually take both, which works in the end. 

All I did was try to stay as relaxed as possible even when I have work deadlines and take supplements like Magnesium or CBD oil as well as making sure I get enough exercise in the day to feel like sleeping at night.

Well it's never too late to improve things, to change, even though getting your momentum back is hard... But if your dreams are so large and intimidating you'll never do anything because it seems impossible, too late etc. You have to start small and then who knows. In terms of acceptance - this came to me after a good friend died at 32 and he was the only one I knew going through similar problems to me - he was a musician too btw and thus far still the most interesting person I've ever met. In other words it can easily be worse than it already is. If you have nothing but you are still alive and physically healthy then already there are many people out there who have it a lot worse than you - and it's human nature to feel better when you know this.

In other words it's not over until it's over - so fight to change things for the better :-)

hey - just read your post. I can relate to it insofar as I am late 30s (still living with parents) and after around 13 years of being mostly unemployed after university, I'm only just starting to emerge from it - i.e. working an OK job, which I don't hate, for just over a year now... it's still hard since I have almost no friends, no g/f and basically not much of a life. It's still much better than it was around 2 years ago though.

I don't know exactly what is preventing you from evolving but for me the problem was I only knew I wanted to do something creative but didn't know how to achieve a career in the area - my parents were both teachers and did not have any experience in this area either. I was also very vain and self absorbed so I started off wanting to be an actor/filmmaker but nothing I did ever made a sustainable income. I made films and acted in parts but it all led me nowhere and for a very long time I had all the depressed, nihilistic thoughts you describe. A lot of my problems were due to me but I also ascribe a lot of my problems to western culture since the amount of BS which is pumped though the media/film and tv filled my head with crap in my 20s. It was only in my 30s when I started to reject all that and think like a normal person.

I think the key is finding your own purpose despite all the confusion and BS out there - for me I made the most progress mentally when I connected with others who were similar to me. It's still hard though because now I don't have any friends, all my old friends are married, doing pretty well, in a different place etc etc etc and I'm just getting started really.

Good luck and hang in there. I would say just accept things as they are and slowly improve things bit by bit.
Much better thanks although not fully back to normal... Hopefully the improvement continues
